events.summary: Military camp removed and Ramakrishna Mission School premises formally handed over.
Nippon Foundation pledged future reconstruction and modernisation of 100 schools.

Government decided to implement university admission quotas for students with disabilities
Matuvil Special Economic Centre reopened and wholesale trading launched
Sri Lanka and India reached initial renewable energy cooperation agreements.
Presidential Fund launched monthly education aid for migrant workers' children.
Lions Club donated waiting chairs to Dickoya Clungn Hospital.

Police medical services division to recruit 25 doctors
Police seek applications to fill 25 medical service vacancies.
Government announced plans for students to receive free Google AI search tools.
Matuvil Special Economic Centre scheduled to reopen after a three-year closure.
Government reportedly authorised overnight commencement of Mannar wind project work.
Opposition members said Mannar wind project work had begun despite calls for suspension.
Wind-turbine components arrived in Mannar as project work resumed.
A company was reportedly awarded the Norochcholai coal-supply tender.
Prime Minister opened the Moon Memorial Botanical Museum at Peradeniya.
Narahenpita Railway Station modernisation works began with private-sector support.
First provincial awareness programme on government digitalisation and AI was held in Kandy.
Wind-power equipment was transported toward Mannar under police protection.
Government announced monthly education assistance for fishermen’s children.

Sri Lanka proposed seeking Indian financing to resume Kankesanthurai Port development.
Jaffna authorities proposed upgrading Old Park’s children’s playground facilities.
Health minister announced consultations on building a modern national testing laboratory.
Seven ADB-funded vehicles handed to health offices for preventive services.
2026 appropriation bill was presented to Parliament.
Sri Lanka Tourism officially recognized an LGBTIQ tourism promotion initiative.
Central Environmental Authority payments became available through GovPay.
Sri Lanka planned publication of its 2025–2035 national policy for older persons.
Teacher training for the new Grade 1 and 6 curriculum is 80 percent complete.
Government planned to complete Central Expressway works by 2028.
Minister cited a six-billion-rupee cost per kilometre caused by project delays.
Provincial AI and digitalisation awareness programme planned for Central Province officials.
Officials planned to reopen Matuvil Economic Centre on September 30.
Commercial bungee-jumping attraction planned for Colombo Lotus Tower by 2026.
India-assisted four-storey ward complex planned for Mullaitivu District General Hospital.
Cabinet approved LKR 1.4 billion allocation for Southern Expressway repairs.
Cabinet approved awarding the repair contract to Access W.K.K. Group.
Court accepted a cost estimate for excavating the Gurukkalmadam human mass grave.
Government plans to restructure CEB into four state-owned companies.
Cabinet approved development of a unified government digital services platform.
Cabinet approved the Artham allowance programme for vulnerable children.
Artham allowance payments began from July 2025.
Cabinet approved backdating eligibility and depositing arrears from January 2025.
Sri Lanka and the EU signed an €8 million biodiversity and waste grant agreement.
Cabinet approved seeking investor proposals for a PPP chlorine plant.
Officials decided to prepare an integrated national fisheries action plan for 2026.
Labour Ministry launched nationwide mobile services for Employees' Provident Fund members.
Government medicine procurement is 80–85% complete to address shortages.
Interviews are underway to recruit 450 drivers and 300 conductors.
Military helicopter, vehicles, and firefighters deployed to control Pettah commercial-area fire.
Minister announced a fully SLTB-owned Lanka Metro Bus Company from October 8.
SLTB technical divisions were instructed to develop seat belts for older buses.
Army organized a seventh annual multisectoral medical camp serving veterans and families.
Gazette disclosed proposed 2026 government expenditure allocations before parliamentary budget presentation.
Special unit opened to investigate foreign employment complaints.
Labour Ministry announced mobile service to resolve EPF disputes nationwide.
Foundation stone laid for a new Kaluwanchikudy Post Office building.
Sri Lanka's BIRDS-X Dragonfly nanosatellite is scheduled for orbital launch.
Sobhadnavi phase two opened and connected 350 MW to the national grid.
Government announced plans to begin petroleum exploration with scientists and experts.
Construction began on six additional oil storage tanks at Kolonnawa.
Cabinet approved construction of a five-storey allied health sciences faculty building.
SLTB plans to recruit 750 female drivers and conductors to address staffing shortages.
The first section of the Kadawatha–Mirigama Central Expressway held its opening ceremony.
Ruwanpura Expressway construction was reported halted.
Construction to Ingiriya was announced for an imminent start.
Reconstruction work on the Southern Expressway had started.
Government plans to open a small additional service centre at Udugawa.
Work began to enable toll payment from Matara after entry at Katunayake.
The minister announced plans to prepare a national highway plan.
United States and Sri Lanka opened an advanced English language laboratory for naval officers.
Former presidential residences will be used for economically beneficial public purposes.
Cabinet approved the timetable for presenting the 2026 Appropriation Bill to Parliament.
Deputy minister announced plans to establish a fisheries port with ice-production facilities.
Government announced a contributory pension scheme for fishing communities nationwide.
U.S. embassy conducted port law and public-private partnership training.
Japan pledged dairy-sector equipment and technology support for Sri Lanka.
Japan pledged drones and surveillance technology for the Sri Lanka Navy.
Southern Province connected all district and divisional secretariats to GovPay.
Public Administration Ministry introduced digital signatures for government officials.
Authorities proposed a public project to control invasive fish in Deduru Oya.
India is studying development of Paruthithurai Port at an estimated cost.
Maradana Railway Station modernisation began under the Clean Sri Lanka programme.
Government said construction of Moratuwa University medical faculty would begin soon.
Treasury allocated Rs. 45 billion to complete Nagoda hospital projects by 2027.
Government expected to construct a new building for Kalassa maternity hospital.
Seventeen earlier projects were abandoned, creating about Rs. 29 billion additional costs.
Authorities released military-held land in Kilinochchi and transferred it to officials.
United States and Sri Lanka completed renovation of Akaragama regional hospital.
Colombo Central Bus Station renovation project held its opening ceremony.
Government targeted establishing 50 multimodal transport stations nationwide by 2029.
The multimodal transport-centre project was initiated under presidential leadership.
President’s Fund scholarships were provided to 28 low-income students in Kandy.
Local Government Week began nationwide under the Reawakening City theme.
Prime Minister pledged funding to complete unfinished classroom buildings in Vanni District.
President launched Colombo Central Bus Station redevelopment under the 50-station national project.
Central Expressway Kadawatha–Mirigama construction was scheduled to resume on September 17.
China Exim Bank provided a reported $500 million loan to restart the expressway project.
Maradana Railway Station renovation is scheduled to begin.
Government plans mandatory pre-departure quality testing for long-distance buses.
Foundation stone ceremony was held for constructing a post office in Balapitiya.
First phase of electronic court system opened at Sri Lanka’s Supreme Court.
Cabinet reportedly approved a plan to privatise state-owned banks.
Indian technical team conducted preliminary studies for proposed Paruthithurai fishing port development.
President’s Fund planned assistance for 360 high-performing Central Province students.
Netherlands approved an additional grant for Sri Lanka’s rural bridges project.
Government allocated funds for nutrition food packages for 160,200 pregnant women.
Cabinet approved ten-month food package assistance for undernourished pregnant and breastfeeding mothers.
Health Ministry launched Arogya mobile medical camps for police officers and families.
Colombo High Court launched card payments for court proceeding fees.
Government allocated nearly Rs. 540 million for Colombo Central Bus Station renovation.
Nallur council proposed Rs. 600 rewards per female stray dog delivered for sterilization.
Government has issued 1,850 land title deeds in Kilinochchi District.
Deputy minister said measures would issue titles for 477 Kilinochchi applications.
Northern officials agreed to expedite Kandarodai pond dredging and develop a permanent mechanism.
Health Ministry recruited 86 dental graduates for limited-practice training.
Chinese financing resumed for stalled Kadawatha–Mirigama Central Expressway construction.
Invasive plants were removed from Kala Wewa-area tanks to restore elephant habitat.
Construction began on a 100-megawatt solar park in Siyambalanduwa.
Sri Lanka Railways planned three-car small trains for rural routes.
Cabinet approved electronically controlled connections between small-train compartments.
Paddy Marketing Board paid farmers Rs. 55 billion under government procurement scheme.
Government purchased over 40,000 metric tonnes under paddy procurement scheme.
Government approved protective nets for fish resources in 250 freshwater reservoirs.
Japan-funded Habarana–Veyangoda transmission project began construction to strengthen electricity distribution.
Northern governor accepted funding request for livestock and sector data collection.
Budget allocated monthly support for children without parents or guardians.
Budget allocated to improve facilities, infrastructure and staffing in 379 children’s homes.
Budget allocated housing and long-term support for care leavers marrying after adulthood.
Budget allocated suitable transport for children required to attend court.
Budget allocated a special neurodevelopment treatment unit at Lady Ridgeway Hospital.
Budget allocated a model daycare centre for early childhood development.
Anti-corruption commission launched a WhatsApp channel for public complaints.
President opened the Northern Province’s first seed coconut production unit.
President initiated preliminary work for a passport office in Jaffna.
President initiated preliminary work for a sports ground in Jaffna.
President initiated preliminary work for a port development project in Jaffna.
Scholarships were awarded to 84 children of registered migrant workers.
Scholarships worth Rs. 50.88 million were scheduled for later distribution.
Phase three of Mayilitti Fisheries Harbour development began.
The 2025 budget allocated Rs. 100 million for Jaffna Public Library digitisation.
The President launched Jaffna Public Library's e-library project.
Construction of Jaffna International Cricket Stadium was scheduled to begin.
Construction of Jaffna International Cricket Stadium began in Mandaitivu.
Jaffna regional passport office opened at the district secretariat complex.
Government allocated Rs. 298 million for Mayilitti harbour facilities.
Jaffna regional passport office was scheduled to open.
Jaffna Public Library e-library project was scheduled to begin.
